title: Prehospital assessment of laboratory parameters using blood gas analysis: Feasibility, clinical relevance and impact on therapeutic decision-making in emergency medical services
summary: The aim of this study is to assess the applicability of preclinical blood gas analysis (BGA) as well as to quantify and describe electrolyte disturbances, blood gas abnormalities, and acid-base imbalances in preclinical emergency patients within the Saarland emergency medical services. Any preclinical treatments based on these findings will be documented, and the usefulness of preclinical blood gas analysis will be evaluated.
conditions: Other disorders of fluid, electrolyte and acid-base balance

interventions.name: All adult patients who were treated preclinically by the emergency physicians of the involved emergency medical vehicles and underwent a blood gas analysis

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Indication for a peripheral venous access and/or arterial blood pressure measurement
Patients with suspected/confirmed disturbances in oxygenation/ventilation
Patients with arrhythmias
Patients with altered consciousness
Patients with suspected metabolic disorders, such as sepsis, acute renal failure
Patients with suspected anemia
Exclusion criteria:
Patients <18 years
No indication for peripheral venous access and/or arterial blood pressure measurement
